Dhul Hulaifah (Abyar Ali): the Miqat for Madinah Pilgrims

ميقات ذو الحليفة (آبار علي) لأهل المدينة

If you travel from Madinah to Makkah for Umrah, you enter Ihram at Dhul Hulaifah (Abyar Ali). Here is where it is, what to do, and how to ask for a stop there on a private transfer.

June 25, 2026
5 min read
Quick Answer

Pilgrims travelling from Madinah to Makkah for Umrah enter Ihram at Dhul Hulaifah (Abyar Ali), about 14 km from Masjid an-Nabawi by road (Saudi Press Agency, March 2026). On a private Madinah to Makkah transfer you can ask for a stop there when you book.

Miqat
Dhul Hulaifah
Also called
Abyar Ali
From Madinah
~14 km
To Makkah
~430 km

Key Insights

  • 1

    What it is: Dhul Hulaifah, also known as Abyar Ali, is the Miqat for people travelling from Madinah towards Makkah. It is the furthest Miqat from Makkah.

  • 2

    Where it is: about 14 km south-west of Masjid an-Nabawi by road, on the road towards Makkah — a short drive from the central Madinah hotels.

  • 3

    What to do there: there is a large mosque at the Miqat with facilities to change and pray. Make your intention (niyyah) for Umrah and enter Ihram before you continue past the Miqat.

  • 4

    By private car: on a Madinah to Makkah transfer, tell us when you book if you want a stop at Dhul Hulaifah and we confirm it as part of the quote. This guide is general transport information, not a religious ruling — follow qualified guidance for your own circumstances.

  • 5

    Ihram essentials: wear the two white seamless garments (men), avoid perfume and cutting hair or nails once in Ihram, and keep a clean backup set.

  • 6

    After the Miqat: continue to Makkah (~430 km, ~4 hours) with prayer and rest stops, then proceed to Masjid al-Haram for Tawaf and Sa'i.

Frequently Asked Questions

Where do pilgrims from Madinah enter Ihram?

At Dhul Hulaifah (Abyar Ali), about 14 km from Masjid an-Nabawi by road, on the route to Makkah. It is the designated Miqat for those travelling from Madinah.

Can a taxi stop at Dhul Hulaifah on the way to Makkah?

You can ask for a stop at Dhul Hulaifah when you book a Madinah to Makkah transfer, and we confirm it as part of the quote. Whether and how to enter Ihram there is a personal religious matter we cannot advise on.

How far is Dhul Hulaifah from Madinah?

Dhul Hulaifah (Abyar Ali) is about 14 km from Masjid an-Nabawi by road — a short drive on the route towards Makkah.
